text:
Yaroslav Askarov stopped 41 of 43 shots, and that is why San Jose walked out of Canadian Tire Centre with a 6-2 win over Ottawa in a game the Senators had mostly controlled. By goals saved above expected, which compares the goals a goalie allowed with what the quality of the shots against him would normally produce, Askarov saved 3.4 more than his workload deserved. Ottawa's Samuel Ersson, by comparison, finished just under even.

The play itself leaned the other way. Ottawa outshot San Jose 43 to 28 and had 92 shot attempts to 55. In expected goals, a measure of chance quality, the Senators led 5.40 to 4.71, and a simulation of replays of every shot gave them a 72 percent chance of winning. Tim Stützle opened the scoring at 6:16 of the first, and Nolan Allan answered before the period ended. San Jose then broke the game open in a 4:18 stretch of the second: Tyler Toffoli scored on the power play, Collin Graf scored shorthanded on a 69 percent chance, and Jacob Trouba made it 4-1. Ottawa dominated the third, out-chancing the Sharks 1.87 to 0.32 in expected goals, but only Jordan Spence's goal at 6:24 came of it.

The Sharks added two more late, a shorthanded goal from Zack Ostapchuk and an empty-looking finish from Ivar Stenberg with 17 seconds left, to turn a lopsided-chances game into a rout. San Jose scored twice shorthanded and went 1 for 2 on the power play, while Ottawa went 0 for 3. The facts here offer no streaks or standings for either side, so what stands is the night itself: the Sharks got a 6-2 road win, and the Senators lost a game their own numbers say they should have won.
